In mathematics, more specifically in [[homotopy theory]], a '''simplicial presheaf''' is a [[presheaf]] on a [[Site (mathematics)|site]] (e.g., the [[Category theory|category]] of [[topological space]]s) taking values in [[simplicial set]]s (i.e., a [[contravariant functor]] from the site to the category of simplicial sets). Equivalently, a simplicial presheaf is a [[simplicial object]] in the category of presheaves on a site. The notion was introduced by [[André Joyal|A. Joyal]] in the 1970s.<ref>{{citation|first=Bertrand|last=Toën|contribution=Stacks and Non-abelian cohomology|title=Introductory Workshop on Algebraic Stacks, Intersection Theory, and Non-Abelian Hodge Theory|publisher=MSRI|year=2002|contribution-url=https://perso.math.univ-toulouse.fr/btoen/files/2015/02/msri2002.pdf}}</ref> Similarly, a '''simplicial sheaf''' on a site is a simplicial object in the category of [[Sheaf (mathematics)|sheaves]] on the site.<ref>{{harvnb|Jardine|2007|loc=§1}}</ref>

== Examples ==

Example: Consider the [[étale site]] of a [[scheme (mathematics)|scheme]] ''S''. Each ''U'' in the site represents the presheaf <math>\operatorname{Hom}(-, U)</math>. Thus, a '''simplicial scheme''', a simplicial object in the site, represents a simplicial presheaf (in fact, often a simplicial sheaf).

Example: Let ''G'' be a presheaf of [[groupoid]]s. Then taking [[nerve (category theory)|nerve]]s section-wise, one obtains a simplicial presheaf <math>BG</math>. For example, one might set <math>B\operatorname{GL} = \varinjlim B\operatorname{GL_n}</math>. These types of examples appear in [[K-theory]].<!--Example: Let a presheaf of groups ''G'' act on a presheaf ''X''; i.e., there are [[group actions]] <math>G(U) \times X(U) \to X(U)</math> for each ''U'' in the site. One then obtains the category <math>EG</math>-->

If <math>f: X \to Y</math> is a [[local weak equivalence]] of simplicial presheaves, then the induced map <math>\mathbb{Z} f: \mathbb{Z} X \to \mathbb{Z} Y</math> is also a local weak equivalence.

== Homotopy sheaves of a simplicial presheaf ==
Let ''F'' be a simplicial presheaf on a site. The '''homotopy sheaves''' <math>\pi_* F</math> of ''F'' are defined as follows. For any <math>f:X \to Y</math> in the site and a 0-simplex ''s'' in ''F''(''X''), set <math>(\pi_0^\text{pr} F)(X) = \pi_0 (F(X))</math> and <math>(\pi_i^\text{pr} (F, s))(f) = \pi_i (F(Y), f^*(s))</math>. We then set <math>\pi_i F</math> to be the sheaf associated with the pre-sheaf <math>\pi_i^\text{pr} F</math>.<!-- discuss hypercovering business -->

== Model structures ==
The category of simplicial presheaves on a site admits several different [[model category|model structure]]s.<!--A map of simplicial presheaves with "local right lifting property" is called a '''hypercover'''.<ref>{{harvnb|Jardine|2007|loc=§ 2}}</ref> (see loc. cit. for the precise definition.)-->

Some of them are obtained by viewing simplicial presheaves as functors 
:<math>S^{op} \to \Delta^{op} Sets</math>
The category of such functors is endowed with (at least) three model structures, namely the [[Injective and projective model structure|projective]], the [[Reedy category|Reedy]], and the [[Injective and projective model structure|injective model structure]]. The weak equivalences / fibrations in the first are maps
:<math>\mathcal F \to \mathcal G</math>
such that 
:<math>\mathcal F(U) \to \mathcal G(U)</math>
is a weak equivalence / fibration of simplicial sets, for all ''U'' in the site ''S''. The injective model structure is similar, but with weak equivalences and cofibrations instead.

== Stack ==
{{main|Stack (mathematics)}}

A simplicial presheaf ''F'' on a site is called a stack if, for any ''X'' and any [[hypercovering]] ''H'' →''X'', the canonical map
:<math>F(X) \to \operatorname{holim} F(H_n)</math>
is a [[weak equivalence (homotopy theory)|weak equivalence]] as simplicial sets, where the right is the [[homotopy limit]] of
:<math>[n] = \{ 0, 1, \dots, n \} \mapsto F(H_n)</math>.

Any sheaf ''F'' on the site can be considered as a stack by viewing <math>F(X)</math> as a constant simplicial set; this way, the category of sheaves on the site is included as a subcategory to the homotopy category of simplicial presheaves on the site. The inclusion functor has a left adjoint and that is exactly <math>F \mapsto \pi_0 F</math>.

If ''A'' is a sheaf of abelian group (on the same site), then we define <math>K(A, 1)</math> by doing classifying space construction levelwise (the notion comes from the [[obstruction theory]]) and set <math>K(A, i) = K(K(A, i-1), 1)</math>. One can show (by induction): for any ''X'' in the site,
:<math>\operatorname{H}^i(X; A) = [X, K(A, i)]</math>
where the left denotes a sheaf cohomology and the right the homotopy class of maps.<!-- A semidirect product of <math>K(A, i)</math>. ....    is called a ''i''-[[gerbe]] with coefficients in ''A''.-->
